text: TAX ANOMALIES.

label: text
text: Canton Special Levy in Operation.

label: text
text: RIVER SHIPPING TRIALS.

label: text
text: "All" Vessels to Submit to Examination?

label: text
text: From Our Own Correspondent.J Samshui (West River), Nov. 24. The special tax bureau of the Nationalist Finance Ministry is now in full operation at Wuchow and there are many anomalies arising out of an impossible situation.

label: text
text: It is well known that the bureau levies 2½ per cent. on ordinary imports and 5 per cent. on luxuries. But for convenience, or some other reason, the staff of the bureau merely asks for half the amount collected by the Chinese Maritime Customs in Hai-kwan taels.

label: text
text: If a part of any shipment comes under the category of "luxuries," the bureau does not trouble to work out its own assessment, merely accepting the figures of the Customs.

label: text
text: Should the Maritime Customs make a seizure of goods not on the manifest, the bureau also puts in a claim for seizure, but the merchandise is only handled in these cases by the Customs. There is no harm in making a formal claim but the question of custody does not arise.

label: text
text:
The staff of the bureau now wear a uniform much similar to that of the Chinese Maritime Customs. The outstanding exception is in the badge.
Instead of the dragon in the middle of the emblem, the Nationalist bureau men have a blue medallion on which is superimposed the white-rayed sun.

label: text
text: Native exporters at Wuchow have been notified by the bureau that the penalty for a false declaration is three years' imprisonment. The staff board the pai's (pontoons serving for wharves), in harbour and scrutinise manifests.

label: text
text:
Liquor Shipment Astray.
I hear that the Custom's Club at Wuchow has not received a shipment of'stores which was sent some' time ago.

label: text
text: Inquiries among the Nationalist Inspection Corps at Do-singled to a belief that the stores had gone astray—to Canton.

label: text
text: Subsequently some stores were delivered through a British steamboat from Hong Kong.

label: text
text: A Portuguese merchant in the liquor business lost altogether 115 cases of wine on one trip, 7 of which were for up-country Roman Catholic missions. This gentleman has now open to him the course of interviewing the Finance Ministry in Canton.

label: text
text: Conditions at Do-sing are different. There the Inspection Corps is only authorised to effect seizures of alleged contraband, but there is no special tax bureau to make collections.

label: text
text: Between Two Fires

label: text
text: The Chinese gunboat which previously left after an encounter with pirates has returned, and is anchored close to the tow, near the special tax bureau.

label: text
text: In this port (Samshui, further down river), merchants are literally between two fires.

label: text
text: Native junks and cargo-boats are told that they must stop for examination at the Nationalist depot, which is outside Samshui harbour limits.

label: text
text: When that examination is over, they proceed to enter port, going a distance of 100 yards or so. But because they have to submit to the bureau they render themselves liable to a fine by the Maritime Customs for “anchoring in transit and breaking bulk.”

label: text
text:
What Compliance Means.
Not every Hong Kong merchant is aware that vessels going from Hong Kong to Vuchow must report to the Customs station at Samshui in case of any stoppage between Whangmoon and Samshui due to fog, breakdown or other unforeseen circumstance of navigation. Failure to do so can result in a smart fine.

label: text
text: But the special tax bureau intends to establish a depot three miles outside Samshul and traders have been informed that all vessels, of whatever nationality, will have to stop and submit to search, Compliance with the tax bureau can only mean running foul of the Customs.

label: paragraph_title
text: MURDER TRIAL.

label: paragraph_title
text:
CHASE BY UNARMED
CONSTABLE.

label: text
text: TO-DAY'S EVIDENCE.

label: text
text: The whole of this morning's proceedings in the Western Market, affray alleged murder case were taken up with the examination and cross-examination of the constable who first gave chase to the prisoner as he ran from the market with a dagger and heavy iron file in his hand.

label: text
text:
Witness detailed the course of the chase along. Chonaught Road and Des Vceux Road Central and said that prisoner twice turned round and, threatening with his weapons, dared witness to come on. Witness was unarmed.
When the prisoner was finally overtaken by other police who had come to the assistance of witness, he still held on to the dagger even when beaten to the earth with a bamboo pole. Witness had to strike his hand repeatedly with a chisel before he would let go of the dagger.

label: text
text: The Crown case against prisoner has not yet been concluded. There are six more witnesses to

label: text
text: be called. It was the original intention of the court to sit until late to-night to finish the case but it is doubtful whether this course will be possible owing to the length of cross-examination.

label: paragraph_title
text: UNUSUAL EXCUSE.

label: paragraph_title
text: $ ^{1} $A $ ^{0} $ WOOD-CUTTER'S SORE

label: text
text: An Indian watchman charged with cutting Government-owned trees, pleaded that he had been told to do so by a Chinese doctor, who directed that the leaves should be boiled and made into a medicine for application to his sore foot. Observing that people were not allowed to go about doing such things, the Magistrate, imposed a fine of $2.

label: text
text: The next case called in the same Court was that of a Chinese charged with a similar offence. Defendant, in denying the charge, hit upon the ingenious excuse that the wood had been cut by another Indian. "Oh I see," said the Magistrate," the last defendant came in very useful to you?" Divisional Inspector Grant proving a previous conviction: His Worship fined the defendant $50 or one month's hard labour.

text: CANTON SEAMEN.

label: paragraph_title
text: Cordon Replaced at British Wharves.

label: text
text: Seamen who claim to have been employed by the Steamboat Co prior to the strike are again causing trouble.

label: text
text: After the resumption of traffic, they picketted the company's wharves in Canton and asked to be reinstated.

label: text
text: Negotiations between intermediaries brought about the withdrawal of the cordon. This week the ex-seamen are alleged to have demanded the dismissal of men of other departments on shipboard, who remained loyal during the boycott.

label: text
text: The truce has broken down as so-called “peaceful pickets” have re-appeared at the approaches to the West Bund, outside the Steamboat Co.'s wharves.

label: text
text: This had the instant effect of causing the number of passengers on one trip to drop below the 100 mark again.

label: text
text: From an unofficial source the "China Mail" learns that there is still a possibility of an understanding being reached by Dec.

label: text
text: Canton, Nov. 25.

label: text
text: It was reported in Chinese circles here yesterday that the negotiations between the Seamens' Union and the Hong Kong, Canton and Macao Steamboat Co., Ltd. (7), for the reinstatement of certain seamen who had left the Company's service during the strike had broken down.

label: paragraph_title
text: PARDONED.

label: paragraph_title
text: JAMES EDWARD ATHERLEY RELEASED.

label: text
text: NOW ON HIS WAY HOME.

label: text
text: The “China Mail” understands that a pardon has been granted James Edward Atherley, who, on January 17 last, was sentenced by the Chief Justice (Sir Henry C. Gollan) to two years' hard labour following a long and sensational trial at the Supreme Court for embezzlement of money the property of his employers, Messrs. Getz's Bros. (of the Orient), Ltd. Mr. Atherley is at present on his way to the United States.

label: text
text: The authorities concerned are reticent with regard to the matter, but as far as can be ascertained, Atherley, who had made several apparently unsuccessful attempts to have his sentence reduced, recently received intimidation that His Excellency the Governor had reviewed the case and that it had been decided that he be released from custody and given a passage to the United States. This was "accordingly done, Atherley being escorted one evening to a trans-Pacific liner by which he proceeded to his native country.

label: paragraph_title
text: COOK HURT.

label: paragraph_title
text:
REPULSE BAY KITCHEN
"SCRAP."

label: text
text: "BRUSHED AGAINST KNIFE."

label: text
text: A'scrap' in the kitchen of the Repulse Bay Hotel had its sequel at the Central Magistracy. this morning, when the No. 1 cook accused a foki of, wounding him with a knife.

label: text
text: Defendant denied having struck the complainant with the knife and asked Mr. Lindsell to believe that the wound was caused by the complainant "brushing up against" the knife when the latter was lying on a table.

label: text
text: Hia Worship decided to hear evidence.

label: text
text: Complainant said that he had ordered the defendant to strain some juice and the latter had refused. Witness pushed the defendant who picked up a butcher's knife and wounded him in the forearm. He could produce no witnesses.

label: text
text: Eugene Fourer, French chef at the Hotel, said that complainant was one of twenty cooks employed in the kitchen at "Repulse Bay Hotel. Witness had had considerable trouble with the defendant in the past and at the time of the assault last night he, witness, was actually engaged in writing out a discharge paper concerning the defendant. He did not actually see the affair, but was called on the scene immediately afterwards.

label: text
text: Defendant said that he could produce three fokls who witnessed the quarrel and His Worship said that he would adjourn the case until to-morrow morning to enable him to do so.

label: paragraph_title
text: THE WEATHER.

label: text
text:
Till noon tomorrow, the weather forecast for Hong Kong, the south China coast and Formosa Channel is: fresh N.E. winds, fine.
At 10.57 a.m. to day the Observatory reported: — Pressure has decreased considerably over central and N.E. Japan and increased slightly from N. Formosa to Chefoo. It is nearly stationary elsewhere. The anti-cyclone has strengthened slightly. A depression is central over the Sea of Japan. It is moving eastward. Fresh monsoon may be expected along the S.E. coast of China and over the China Sea.

label: paragraph_title
text: RUHR PLOT.

label: text
text:
Another War Europe
Missed.

label: text
text: STARTLING REVELATIONS.

label: paragraph_title
text: Murder of All Foreign Troops!

label: text
text: Berlin, Nov. 25.

label: text
text: Following the admission of Herr Gessler, Minister of Defence, in the Reichstag, that at the time of the Ruhr invasion, German Nationalist organisations contemplated forcible ejection of the invaders, it now appears that officers of the old German Army and extremists at one time planned to have "Sicilian vespers" in Germany in which all foreign troops would be murdered. They also proposed to form an army of 60,000 disciplined workmen in the Ruhr, while Russia's aid was also to be enlisted in "the fight for freedom."

label: text
text: The extremist leaders prepared to abandon Germany to the enemy as far as the river Elbe where a final stand would be made.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text:
War Guilt.
Berlin, Nov. 25.

label: text
text: The Reichstag has rejected the non-confidence motion lodged by the Communists and extreme Nationalists. A resolution by the non-Socialist parties requesting the Government to examine whether the League Covenant offered a possibility of referring the investigation of war guilt to an international court of arbitration was adopted against the votes of the Socialists and Communists.

label: paragraph_title
text: COAL TERMS.

label: text
text: SCOTLAND FALLING INTO LINE.

label: text
text: NOW 428,000 MEN BACK.

label: text
text: London; Nov. 26.

label: text
text: Satisfactory progress is being made in Scotland towards settlement of the coal dispute.

label: text
text: Matters have been left in the hands of a small joint. committee which will submit the terms to each side for ratification.

label: text
text: Officials of the Lancashire and Cheshire Miners' Federation have discussed terms with the coal owners. These will be submitted to the miners' conference in London to-morrow.—Reuter.

label: text
text: 428,000 miners were working today.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: Eight Hour Day.

label: text
text: The Scottish coalowners' and miners' representatives have arrived at an agreement which will be submitted to both sides.

label: text
text: It is understood that the agreement provides for an eight hour day and a nominal minimum wage of $98.4d.

label: text
text: The Northumberland Miners' Council has decided to recommend acceptance of the owners' terms, including the 7½ hour shift for hewers and 8 hours for other workers.

label: text
text: After a lengthy conference at Cannock Chase the coalowners and miners at Birmingham failed to reach agreement, but the great majority of the men are working. —Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: SEX OF A CARP.

label: text
text: DISPUTE LEADS TO KICK IN SPLEEN.

label: text
text: A quarrel over the sex of a carp at a stall in the Central Market had its sequel in Major Willson's Court at the Central Magistracy this morning, when a Chinese stall-holder was charged with assault and causing serious bodily harm to a customer. Inspector Marks informed the Magistrate that the complainant was in hospital suffering from a kick in the spleen and asked for an adjournment for a week. Defendant was accordingly remanded in custody.

label: text
text: "You are Government servants, it is your business to keep the peace, not to break it," said Mr. Lindsell to three Sanitary Board coolies charged with street fighting at the Central Magistracy this morning. His Worship fined each man $3.
